newsitem.title: ITALY: Thieves shoot Naples man carrying $10-police.
newsitem.headline: Thieves shoot Naples man carrying $10-police.

text.p: A Naples man waiting for a bus to take him to work was shot in the leg by two youths angered that the wallet they had stolen from him contained only 16,000 lire ($10.50), police said on Tuesday.
The shooting was the latest of a string of petty crimes gone violent in Naples, the largest city in Italy's poor south.
Police said two youths on a motorbike confronted the 45-year-old plumber at a bus stop on Monday and demanded his wallet at gunpoint.
They shouted insults when they discovered it contained only a small amount of cash.
The man, thinking the gun might be fake, answered back and the youth holding the gun shot him in the leg, police said.
A passing motorist took the man to hospital where he had surgery and was reported in good condition. No arrests have been made.

Last July, a 19-year-old man was fatally shot when a gang of youths tried to steal his motorbike. The shooting sparked anger among residents of Naples and a few weeks later police had to intervene to rescue two other thieves when an angry mob tried to stop them from stealing a motor scooter.
